## Goal
`system_browser` (`doctor.py:197-208`) looks for Edge only under `%ProgramFiles(x86)%` and `%ProgramFiles%` (`doctor.py:191-192`). Edge can also be installed for one user under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Edge\Application\msedge.exe`, and a 32-bit Python sees `%ProgramFiles%` as the x86 folder, so the 64-bit folder is only reachable via `%ProgramW6432%`. On such PCs the doctor says "no Chrome, Edge or Playwright Chromium found" although Edge is there. Add those paths for Edge (and `%ProgramW6432%` for Chrome too), keep the order (Program Files first), and make the test prove path expansion with a fake environment and a fake file tree. Linux and macOS lists are unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. With fake env values pointing at a `tmp_path` tree containing `Microsoft/Edge/Application/msedge.exe` only under the per-user path, `system_browser("msedge")` returns that path on a simulated win32 (monkeypatch `sys.platform` and `os.path.expandvars` to a substitution of `%NAME%`).
2. With files under several candidates, the first in list order wins (Program Files before per-user).
3. A candidate that is a directory, or a missing file, is skipped; an env variable that is not set leaves `%NAME%` unexpanded and is skipped, never an exception.
4. `_CHANNEL_PATHS["msedge"]["win32"]` and `["chrome"]["win32"]` contain exactly the old entries plus the new ones (table test), and the linux/darwin entries are byte-identical to before.
5. `check_browser` on simulated win32 reports "system browser (msedge)" when only the per-user Edge exists, and the existing messages in the other branches are unchanged.
6. No real browser is started; no subprocess; `tmp_path` only.
